cost: body/paragraphs/sentences linear in materialized bytes/tokens; heading search may revisit normalization and scan up to O(headings*lines*line length). CoNLL assembly allocates full output; annotation training/inference and DB loading are additional opaque costs.
description: Synthetic book segmentation and corpus orchestration
forward: body selects lines between first ordered Gutenberg markers and removes CR endings. split removes illustration lines, uses TOC minimum-indent entries with normalized ignores and ordered blank-surrounded matching headings, or title/start/end single section, then normalized skip. paragraphs collapse whitespace and label head/lg/p. sentences emits half-open token spans after terminal/closers unless next starts lowercase/internal punctuation. run trains annotator, writes all CoNLL files/index then loads sequentially.
inverse: Missing/out-of-order Gutenberg markers cannot produce body. Missing TOC entries/start/end or empty retained tale cannot return split success. A terminal followed by lowercase cannot alone force a boundary under the current rule.

Paragraph output admits all original line/whitespace layouts that collapse identically and satisfy block classification. Sentence span output constrains terminal/closer and following-character predicates, not token lexical identities. Raw book, removed illustrations and skipped sections are not recoverable.

Only minimum indent TOC items survive before ignore filtering; headings must appear in TOC order surrounded by blanks. Case/curly single quote/whitespace normalization creates equivalence classes, not fuzzy matching.

A one-line all-uppercase alphabetic paragraph is head; otherwise multiple wholly indented lines are lg; all remaining are p. Classification uses pre-collapse line count/indentation, so equal output text can have different block labels.
At terminal index i, j advances through terminal/closer run. If next is lowercase or ,;:-–— then no split, otherwise emit [start,j). Final residual suffix is emitted once.

run creates output directory before training, writes per-book files and index before DB loads. Later failure leaves earlier files and possibly loaded books. It is not an all-books transaction and was not invoked.
limitations: Finite helper/fixture evidence only; no DuckDB integration or SQL semantics
Partial syntax projection; no macro expansion or full semantic proof
No executable approximate profile or speedup claim
state: Sentence spans partition token indices in order for nonempty tokens; empty list yields no spans. Paragraph text loses original whitespace. conllu disambiguates equal slugs with -n, emits document metadata on first actual sentence and paragraph markers per tokenized paragraph; real annotator/corpus execution is outside evidence.
